basics.name: Shubham Joshi
basics.label: AI Engineer
basics.summary: I build multi-agent LLM systems for production: requests routed by complexity, answers grounded in deterministic tools, and prompts tuned against an eval harness.
bio: I'm an AI engineer. My work comes down to one question: how do you make LLM systems dependable enough to put in front of real users?

At String Ventures (Sutra.ai) I design multi-agent systems on Google ADK, with specialized agents for intake, forecasting and weather hazards, working over live data. Requests are routed by complexity so simple questions stay fast and cheap. The agents decide what to compute and deterministic code does the computing, which is how the numbers stay correct.

Before that, at InfoOrigin, I took natural-language analytics to production: an NL2SQL and RAG platform across 200+ database schemas, covering retrieval, query routing, streaming and multi-session conversations. It cut manual analysis effort by over 80%.

highlights.title: Multi-agent orchestration
highlights.text: Architected a hierarchical LLM system on Google ADK coordinating 8+ specialized agents (intake router, forecast sub-orchestrator, hazard, lightning and hail specialists), with LiteLLM cross-provider failover.

highlights.title: Cost-aware routing
highlights.text: A 3-tier complexity router maps each request to the right model and reasoning effort, and a deterministic fast-path gate collapses simple queries to a single LLM call to cut latency and token cost.

highlights.title: Grounded numbers
highlights.text: Designed the function-calling layer: agents select transforms while a registry-driven engine computes 108 weather attributes across 7 summarizer types over live FLASH Weather AI data, eliminating numeric hallucination in responses.

highlights.title: Eval-first prompting
highlights.text: Built a 60-query natural-language eval harness with deterministic pass/fail checks, and tuned prompts, routing signals and complexity tiers to a 60/60 pass rate.

highlights.title: Conversation memory
highlights.text: Added LLM-based memory that summarizes multi-turn context for cross-session continuity.

highlights.title: NL2SQL and RAG platform
highlights.text: Built and productionized a platform for natural-language querying and report generation across 200+ database schemas, serving 70+ queries daily, using Qdrant, semantic search and LLMs for query routing.

highlights.title: Analytics automation
highlights.text: Automated end-to-end analytics workflows with streaming APIs, multi-session conversation management and context retrieval, reducing manual analysis effort by over 80%.

highlights.title: UAV surveillance
highlights.text: Designed a surveillance system for UAVs to improve stability and accuracy, using data-driven insights to enhance performance.

highlights.title: Chatbot and recommendations
highlights.text: Developed a chatbot and a recommendation system for a startup using LLMs and transformers.

projects.name: CRM MCP Server
projects.description: A production MCP server in Go that lets external AI agents work inside a multi-tenant CRM, with a person approving every write.
highlights: Secured with OAuth 2.0 and role-based tool permissions, enabling agents to run a full 5-step prospecting workflow end to end.
Agent research is stored outside the CRM first and only written in after a person reviews and approves it.
Automated reports flag incomplete records, cutting manual data entry.

projects.name: Portfolio Agent
projects.description: The AI agent you can talk to on this site's home page. It answers questions about my work from structured data, and shows every step it takes as it works.
highlights: A deterministic gate answers fixed questions with no LLM call. Everything else goes to a streaming tool-use loop on Gemini, capped at 3 turns.
Four read-only tools over structured data keep answers grounded, with BM25 retrieval over atomic facts.
If the model fails, answers fall back to search instead of an error, and an eval harness checks behaviour with deterministic pass/fail cases.

projects.name: Contract Risk Intelligence
projects.description: A six-agent workflow that reads a legal contract and produces a plain-English risk report, with a final risk score and questions to ask before signing.
highlights: Clause, risk, obligation, plain-language, negotiation and summary agents run as a deterministic pipeline.
Only the clause agent reads the full document. Every downstream agent works from the compact clause list, which keeps token usage low.
The analysis core is plain LangChain and Pydantic, with the NeMo Agent Toolkit as a thin layer on top for workflow and tracing.
flow: Risk, obligation, plain-language and negotiation agents

projects.name: Conversational RAG Agent
projects.description: A multi-turn RAG agent with LangGraph tool-calling, conversation memory and Qdrant retrieval, measured with RAGAS.
highlights: A LangGraph router decides between retrieval and direct generation, with memory carried across turns.
MMR retrieval over Qdrant, and FastAPI endpoints for ingest, chat, token streaming over SSE, sessions and evaluation.
Evaluated with RAGAS on a curated testset and packaged with Docker Compose.

projects.name: Nichi-Tex
projects.description: Matches a resume against a job description, finds the skill gaps and generates a tailored LaTeX resume.
highlights: Parses PDF and DOCX resumes and job descriptions into structured data.
Semantic matching with sentence transformers, plus gap analysis with actionable recommendations.
Exposes the pipeline through FastAPI and outputs ATS-friendly LaTeX.

projects.name: Bill Converter
projects.description: A hybrid PDF-to-Excel invoice converter with a free rules-based mode and a Gemini-powered Pro mode.
highlights: Free mode uses pdfplumber and regex, with an OCR.space fallback for scans.
Pro mode hands pdfplumber output to Gemini for extraction.

projects.name: Billventory
projects.description: A billing and inventory app for small businesses with AI built into the daily workflow.
highlights: Dashboard for sales, purchases and profit, with stock tracked automatically from transactions.
Upload an invoice image to auto-fill forms, ask a chat assistant business questions and get monthly AI reports.

projects.name: TextGen
projects.description: A multimodal LLM tool that generates step-by-step instructions from screenshots.
highlights: React frontend with Google Gemini handling image recognition and text generation.

projects.name: Clod
projects.description: Generates personalized cold emails from a job description link.
highlights: Extracts key details with Groq, matches relevance with ChromaDB and drafts with Llama 3.1, with adjustable tone.

principles.title: Let models decide, let code compute
principles.text: LLMs are good at choosing what to do and bad at arithmetic. So agents select the transform and a deterministic engine does the math, which removed numeric hallucination across 108 weather attributes.

principles.title: Evals before opinions
principles.text: A prompt change isn't better until it passes. I write deterministic pass/fail checks first, then tune prompts, routing signals and complexity tiers against them. One 60-query suite went to 60/60 this way.

principles.title: Not every question needs the big model
principles.text: A complexity router picks the model and reasoning effort for each request, and a deterministic gate collapses simple queries to a single LLM call. Both cut latency and token cost.

principles.title: Design for failure
principles.text: Providers go down and models misbehave. Cross-provider failover, capped agent loops and fallbacks mean a bad moment produces a useful answer rather than an error page.

principles.title: Agents propose, people approve
principles.text: When an agent can write to a real system, its output waits outside that system until a person has reviewed it. Automation saves the time, and a human keeps the accountability.

principles.title: Memory is a design decision
principles.text: Conversations need context, but not all of it forever. I summarize multi-turn history with an LLM so agents keep continuity across sessions without dragging the full transcript along.
